chapters.heading: UNITED STATES CAPITOL POLICE REFORM AND ACCOUNTABILITY

sections.heading: Chief of the United States Capitol Police
paragraphs: (a) There shall be a Chief of the United States Capitol Police, who shall serve as the principal executive and operational officer of the Capitol Police.
(b) The Chief shall be appointed by majority vote of the Capitol Police Board.
(c) The Chief may be removed by majority vote of the Capitol Police Board.
(d) The Chief may also be removed by concurrent resolution of Congress.

(e) Where misconduct, neglect, abuse of authority, incapacity, failure of command, refusal to carry out lawful security directions, failure to provide necessary coverage, or failure to protect congressional proceedings primarily concerns one House, its Members, its officers, its proceedings, or its controlled spaces, that House may by resolution make findings concerning the Chief, declare loss of confidence in the Chief, request or require review by the Capitol Police Board, direct the relevant Sergeant at Arms to transmit the matter to the Board, or require the Board to meet and vote on whether the Chief should be removed, suspended, limited, disciplined, or otherwise subject to corrective action.
(f) A resolution of one House under the preceding subsection shall not, by itself, remove the Chief from office as Chief of the United States Capitol Police.

(g) Where the House of Representatives determines that the Chief has failed, refused, or is unable to protect House-controlled areas, House proceedings, Members of the House, officers of the House, House employees, House witnesses, invited guests of the House, or other persons or functions connected to the official business of the House, the House may by resolution suspend or limit the Chief’s authority within House-controlled areas for the duration of the failure, refusal, incapacity, emergency, or other stated security need.

(h) Where the Senate determines that the Chief has failed, refused, or is unable to protect Senate-controlled areas, Senate proceedings, Senators, officers of the Senate, Senate employees, Senate witnesses, invited guests of the Senate, or other persons or functions connected to the official business of the Senate, the Senate may by resolution suspend or limit the Chief’s authority within Senate-controlled areas for the duration of the failure, refusal, incapacity, emergency, or other stated security need.

(i) A suspension or limitation imposed by one House under this section shall be confined to the controlled spaces, proceedings, persons, or security needs of that House and shall not permanently alter the command structure of the Capitol Police, remove the Chief from office, or limit the authority of the Capitol Police Board to remove, discipline, restore, limit, or otherwise act concerning the Chief.

(j) During a suspension or limitation under this section, the relevant Sergeant at Arms may temporarily direct available Capitol Police officers assigned to that House’s controlled spaces as necessary to protect that House, preserve order, secure proceedings, control access, respond to emergencies, escort witnesses or guests, remove disorderly persons, and carry out lawful security directions.

(k) The relevant Sergeant at Arms shall notify the Capitol Police Board as soon as practicable after exercising authority under this section and shall provide the Board with the findings, reasons, duration, affected spaces, and security actions taken.

(l) The Capitol Police Board shall review any action taken by one House under this section as soon as practicable and may remove the Chief, suspend the Chief, limit the Chief’s duties, restore the Chief’s authority, direct corrective action, or take any other lawful action within the Board’s authority. (m)The Chief shall command the day-to-day operations of the Capitol Police, supervise officers and employees, implement policies approved by the Board, direct patrols, coordinate protective services, manage training, issue operational regulations, maintain records, respond to emergencies, and perform any other duty assigned by this Act, by the Board, or by lawful regulation.
(n) The Chief shall remain subject to the oversight, regulations, directives, and lawful orders of the Board.

(o) The Chief may issue regulations, general orders, directives, and procedures governing the administration and operation of the Capitol Police, including access to the United States Capitol Buildings and Grounds, security operations, officer conduct, emergency response, interagency coordination, protective assignments, arrests, removals, detentions, use of force, records, discipline, training, deployment outside jurisdiction, and any other operational matter necessary to carry out this Act.

(p) Any regulation, general order, directive, or procedure issued by the Chief shall be consistent with this Act, the rules of either House, lawful orders of either House, lawful directions of the Board, and the authority of the Speaker, President pro tempore, Presiding Officer, and Sergeant at Arms of either House over that House’s proceedings, chamber, officers, privileges, discipline, and controlled spaces.

(q) The Chief shall submit any major regulation, general order, directive, or procedure to the Board for review. The Board may approve, amend, suspend, disapprove, or require revision of any such regulation, general order, directive, or procedure.

(r) The Board may require prior approval before the Chief issues any regulation, general order, directive, or procedure that substantially affects use of force, arrest authority, detention procedure, access to either chamber, deployment outside jurisdiction, interagency coordination, protective services, officer discipline, public access rules, or the rights, privileges, safety, or official duties of Members of Congress.

(s) The Chief shall not enter into any agreement with an executive department, executive agency, State, local government, foreign entity, private entity, or outside organization affecting the jurisdiction, authority, command, personnel, data, records, equipment, funding, or operations of the Capitol Police without approval of the Board, except where immediate assistance is necessary during an emergency.

(t) Where immediate assistance is requested or received during an emergency without prior approval of the Board, the Chief shall notify the Board as soon as practicable and shall submit a written report explaining the emergency, the assistance requested or received, the outside entity involved, the officers deployed, the actions taken, the duration of the assistance, and any continuing effect on Capitol Police operations.

(u) The Chief shall promptly notify the Board, the Speaker, the President pro tempore, and the relevant Sergeant at Arms of any major security incident, emergency deployment, lockdown, evacuation, arrest of a Member of Congress, detention of a Member of Congress, threat to a Member of Congress, use of force resulting in injury or death, removal from congressional proceedings, request for outside law enforcement assistance, or incident that materially affects the safety, access, privileges, or official duties of either House.

(v) The Chief shall maintain accurate records concerning arrests, removals, detentions, uses of force, complaints, officer discipline, emergency actions, protective assignments, outside deployments, interagency assistance, access restrictions, and major security incidents. (w)The Chief shall provide records, reports, testimony, explanations, and other information to the Board upon request.

(x) The Chief shall ensure that all officers and employees of the Capitol Police are trained on this Act, the rules and privileges of each House, use of force, de-escalation, lawful removals, arrests, detentions, emergency response, chamber access, protection of Members, political neutrality, and any other subject required by the Board.

(y) The Chief shall not use the Capitol Police, or permit the Capitol Police to be used, for any political purpose, personal purpose, retaliatory purpose, or purpose unrelated to the protection of Congress, the enforcement of law, the preservation of order, or the lawful duties of the Capitol Police.

(z) Nothing in this section shall be construed to permit the Chief to override the lawful authority of either House, the Speaker, the President pro tempore, the Presiding Officer of either House, the Sergeant at Arms of either House, or the Board.
